authority: CEO R328 — identify the single remaining evidence bottleneck for each candidate
principle: A package is BUYER_SENDABLE when it tells a company: what the technology is, what evidence exists, what is uncertain, what would prove it, what would kill it, and what it costs to find out. It does NOT need to be 'working' — it needs to be credible and evaluable.

P-01.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — no bench prototype exists. The 1D/3D computational model agrees (16%), but real valve dynamics, sensor performance, and multi-segment hardware are untested.
P-01.rationale: The package is BUYER_SENDABLE because it contains: (1) computational model verified by external 3D solver, (2) V0 bench prototype design ($3-5K COTS), (3) exact test protocol, (4) pass/fail/ambiguous decision rules, (5) economics, (6) differentiation. A company can evaluate this without trusting our narrative — they can reproduce the computation AND commission the bench test.

P-02.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — 47.3% ICP reduction is MODELLED only. Real valve dynamics may differ.
P-02.bottleneck: Bench: adaptive vs fixed valve in mock CSF loop
P-02.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: the package tells the buyer exactly what to build, what to measure, what PASS/FAIL means, and what decision follows. The computational model is reproducible. The decisive experiment is $10-20K. The buyer doesn't need to trust the 47.3% — they need to test it.

P-04.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — enzyme kinetics in CSF are unknown. The 100% Aβ clearance is MODELLED.
P-04.bottleneck: In vitro: NEP-coated catheter in Aβ-spiked aCSF
P-04.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: complete wet-lab protocol, equipment list, sample size, pass/fail thresholds, decision consequences. The buyer can commission this at any biomaterials lab.

P-07.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — safety floor drainage mechanism not tested in real geometry.
P-07.bottleneck: Bench: obstruction simulation with/without safety floor
P-07.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: bench protocol defined, $5-10K, clear pass/fail. Simple experiment.

P-09.decisive_uncertainty: CONCEPTUAL — the transduction molecule has not been designed. This is not a physical validation problem; it's a design problem.
P-09.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: the package tells the buyer exactly what molecule properties are needed (sensitivity >1 mmHg, response <0.1s, CSF stability >30 days), what design space to search (piezoelectric/mechanochromic/hydrogel), what the go/no-go criteria are, and what it costs. A pharma company can evaluate this as a research direction.

P-10.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — phase-change dynamics in real valve assembly. The 0.34s is MODELLED from thermal scaling.
P-10.bottleneck: Bench: n-octadecane valve response time measurement
P-10.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: bench protocol, $5-10K, clear pass (<5s)/fail (≥6s). The computational repair is reproducible. The buyer tests the real valve.

P-11.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — phage stability on Ti surface in CSF. Biofilm prevention in realistic S. aureus challenge.
P-11.bottleneck: In vitro: phage-coated vs uncoated in S. aureus biofilm assay
P-11.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: microbiology protocol, $10-20K, clear pass (<20% biofilm)/fail (≥50%). Any microbiology lab can run this.

P-12.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — Cathepsin D kinetics in CSF. Tau substrate accessibility.
P-12.bottleneck: In vitro: Cathepsin D-coated catheter in tau-spiked aCSF
P-12.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: enzyme assay protocol, $15-25K, clear pass (≥80% clearance)/fail (<50%).

P-13.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL (DATA) — prediction accuracy on real patient data. The model exists but hasn't seen real clinical data.
P-13.bottleneck: Retrospective: train on shunt patient dataset, test on held-out cohort
P-13.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: the buyer (likely a hospital or device company with clinical data access) can run the retrospective analysis. Protocol, endpoints (AUC ≥0.80, lead time ≥12h), and decision consequences are defined.

P-15.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — cardiac harvesting in target implant location. The 10 μW P50 is from published literature, not measured in our geometry.
P-15.bottleneck: Bench: cardiac harvesting measurement in target implant geometry
P-15.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: 96-point operating envelope, published cross-check, buyer-executable assumptions, decisive experiment ($5-10K). The buyer can reproduce the computation AND measure the harvest.

P-16.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — experimental tissue measurement at 940nm. MCX (GPU) not yet run but PyTissueOptics is sufficient for computational validation.
P-16.bottleneck: Bench: 940nm LED + tissue phantom + PV cell
P-16.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: ACTUAL PyTissueOptics executed (pip-installable, reproducible). Verified range 1.0-1.4 mW/cm². Decisive bench experiment ($2-5K). The buyer can reproduce the MC AND run the bench test.

P-20.decisive_uncertainty: PHYSICAL — IL-10 release from PLGA in CSF-like conditions. Glycan surface stability.
P-20.bottleneck: In vitro: PLGA-IL-10 coated catheter in aCSF, 30-day release measurement
P-20.rationale: BUYER_SENDABLE: complete wet-lab protocol, $5-10K, clear pass/fail/ambiguous, buyer decision tree. The computational model predicts 2468 ng/cm²/day (24,680x above threshold). The buyer tests whether reality matches.

P-14.rationale: Negative knowledge package. A company can inspect this to avoid the CSF-yield-matching approach. Reusable knowledge: SNR < 2 → kill before manufacturing.

P-17.rationale: Negative knowledge package. A company can inspect this to avoid cellular surfaces in CSF. Reusable knowledge: endothelial cells die in CSF.

P-19.rationale: Negative knowledge package. A company can inspect the 11-round falsification chain. Reusable knowledge: distributed channels don't beat single at matched conductance.

summary.note: ALL remaining bottlenecks are PHYSICAL/CONCEPTUAL/DATA. The machine has exhausted what computation can resolve. Reality is now the bottleneck (Article XXXIV). Every active candidate has a defined decisive experiment that a company can commission.
